deals.evidence: a venda de 46% das ações do clube ao V Sports por 5,5 milhões de euros
deals.headline: Members approve sale of 46% of Vitória SC SAD to V Sports for EUR 5.5m
deals.summary: An extraordinary general meeting approved (966 for, 136 against) the sale of 46% of the SAD to Nassef Sawiris's V Sports fund for EUR 5.5m; V Sports also committed EUR 2m of infrastructure investment and a credit line of up to EUR 20m at 5.5%.

deals.evidence: uma linha de crédito até 20 milhões de euros para investimentos no futebol, com juro de apenas 5,5%
deals.headline: V Sports credit line of up to EUR 20m for Vitória SC football
deals.summary: Part of the V Sports agreement: a credit line of up to EUR 20m at 5.5% with no fees; guarantees changed from club shares to rents, ticketing and membership dues for the first EUR 7m, plus TV rights and player registrations. Whether it was drawn is not stated.

deals.evidence: ficando a V Sports com uma posição de 29%
deals.headline: UEFA multi-club rules cut V Sports to 29% of Vitória SC SAD
deals.summary: After a UEFA review of V Sports' links with Vitória and Aston Villa, the club used its pre-emption right to take a qualified majority (67.87%) and V Sports was left with 29%, with no change to the EUR 5.5m deal value; V Sports' directors Nassef Sawiris and Wes Edens left the SAD board.

deals.headline: Apollo fund loan secured on Vitória SC's TV rights
deals.source_name: Vitória SC – Futebol, SAD Relatório e Contas 2024/25
deals.summary: The SAD's 2024/25 accounts show a loan from the Apollo fund (EUR 2.51m outstanding at 30 June 2025, due within a year), secured on television revenue, which the report says is anticipated and almost entirely committed to servicing it. An MSD loan is also mentioned without an amount. Origination date and original size not stated.

notes: Every figure is from the club's own site and the 2024/25 accounts (season ending 30 June 2025). The accounts PDFs are behind a bot check on vitoriasc.pt, so a re-fetch may need cookies, and PDF text extraction puts stray spaces inside some numbers (e.g. '7 .610.319,29'). Revenue is the SAD's sales and services; player sales of EUR 49.5m gross (EUR 27.54m net gain) are booked separately under other income. Net result 2024/25: EUR 7,610,319.29 profit. Equity was still negative (EUR -24.0m) at 30 June 2025. The report's 'passivo líquido' of EUR 47.32m is liabilities net of short-term assets, not net debt, so net_debt is null. The ownership page says 67.84% for the club; the June 2023 statement said 67.87%. The club bought back the shares held by Mário Andrade Ferreira's MAF in 2023 as part of the V Sports deal (no price stated). The investor_type for V Sports is private_equity as the nearest fit, since the club calls it a fund. Not found: valuation (the SAD is not listed and no Forbes figure exists), shirt sponsor for 2025/26, chief executive (the SAD has no named CEO), social follower counts, and the Apollo and MSD loans' original size and date. The leadership is the 2026-2029 term (president Rui Rodrigues).
ownership_summary: The football company Vitória Sport Clube – Futebol, SAD is 67.84% owned by the member-owned club Vitória Sport Clube, 29.00% by V Sports (the fund of Nassef Sawiris and Wes Edens, owners of Aston Villa), with 3.16% held by other shareholders. V Sports agreed in March 2023 to buy 46% for EUR 5.5m; in June 2023, after UEFA multi-club rules, the stake was cut to 29% and V Sports gave up its board seats.
